title: Anduril Scores $2.9B Navy Contract as Luckey Joins Pentagon
key_facts: Anduril said on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 it will invest $3.7 billion in a new shipyard in Baltimore County, Maryland, to build parts for Virginia-class submarines.
The Navy awarded Anduril a contract worth up to $2.9 billion for submarine components, with payments tied to production outcomes and Anduril carrying most of the execution risk.
Together they are valued at up to $6.6 billion, per the company.
The plant, Arsenal-2, is expected to be running by the end of the decade, with 3,100 direct jobs.
Anduril is already building a California facility for Virginia-class parts such as torpedo tubes.
General Dynamics' Electric Boat and Huntington Ingalls jointly build the submarines.
CNBC's headline says the award came days after Palmer Luckey joined a Pentagon weapons group (text not read).
quote_evidence: The investment and associated contract, together valued at up to $6.6 billion, come amid a broader push by the United States and its allies to expand arms production following Russia's invasion of Ukraine and conflicts in the Middle East.
"It's really the government buying the results of what we're able to produce from the facility that we've invested in," said Christian Brose, chief strategy officer at Anduril.
why_it_matters_hint: A start-up is taking on much of the cost and risk of building submarine parts for the US Navy.
